svg.title: Failure timelines: receiver down, partition, issuer crash
svg.desc: Three timelines for one invalidated key. Panel A: a receiver node crashes and restarts; its cache is empty so nothing stale remains. Panel B: a link from the issuer to one receiver is cut; the receiver serves the old value until the link heals and the repair worker delivers the owed invalidation. Panel C: the issuer crashes after answering 204 before the receiver acknowledged; the owed invalidation is lost and the receiver stays stale until the entry expires.
svg.text: A. Receiver B crashes (node down), then restarts. Status: TESTED in parts (see text)
Nothing stale survives because B's cache is in memory. Risk is for a B that is ALIVE but cut off (panel B).
Debts are bounded per peer; on overflow they collapse to a tenant flush, then to a full flush of B.
If G's ledger is empty because G also died, B has no stale data to lose anyway.
Heartbeats do not trigger Suspect: only a failed data-path call or /api/control changes the state.
B. Link G to B is cut, B stays alive and serving. Status: TESTED (loopback fault proxy, debug build)
Test test_m3_04a_missed_fanout_repaired_by_antientropy_within_bound held the fault 2000 ms; B stayed HIT v1.
After healing it asserted convergence within 250 + 300 + 250 = 800 ms (interval + delivery budget + margin).
The 800 ms is a test-derived bound for one key, 3 gateways, loopback, a debug build. It is not a product guarantee.
With a PERMANENT cut there is no bound except the entry's own freshness lifetime (60 s only if the origin gave none).
No leader and no quorum exist, so no split brain; instead the two sides simply diverge until repair.
The HTTP GET path never looks at the node state, so a Suspect B keeps serving HITs.
C. Issuer G crashes with owed invalidations. Status: REPRODUCED in a sandbox; fix NOT integrated
Sandbox run (docs/research/m3_durability, debug, loopback, Windows): B never converged in 10 s (89 to 91 stale polls); origin max-age=120.
Negative control (G not killed) converged in 231 to 337 ms. Receiver B cannot detect that G lost anything.
Bound on staleness: the entry's freshness lifetime. That is 60 s only when the origin sends no freshness data, and
PHANTOM_DEFAULT_TTL_MS is not wired; an origin max-age of hours has no gateway ceiling. No test in the main tree covers this.
Source: m3_durability/reproduction_report.md; router.rs; main.rs shutdown path (no router stop or drain call).
